rationale: Under a preregistered paraphrase gate (Spearman rho >= 0.85 and mean |dp| <= 0.05 per feature, 200 rows), all 7 predictive TESS features passed (tightest rho 0.866, |dp| 0.0465) but 2 of 3 label-echo features failed, the paraphrase effect (mean |dp| 0.0250) was 4.4x the same-wording re-ask noise (0.0056), and on the separately preregistered Kepler transfer 3 of 6 predictive features failed rho (0.841, 0.828, 0.651) (RESULTS.md §6; RESULTS_KEPLER.md KG3 table).

With zero-shot Laya grounding plan steps (accept at p >= 0.4 with a word match or p >= 0.8, else lexical fallback, else LLM replan), plan-and-execute matched budget-matched ReAct (88.8% vs 92.0%, paired -3.2 pp [-7.7, +1.2]) at 83.6% fewer input tokens over 2,400 runs, but Laya was not significantly better than word-overlap matching (+2.3 pp [-0.2, +5.0]), declined every candidate on unlabeled TodoMVC toggles, and its post-action check never fired in 403 steps (Tables 1-2, Sec. 6-7).

Unmodified Laya on Whisper ASR transcripts reached Macro F1 89.2% / AUROC 94.9% on 282 held-out robocalls and the author-adapted direct-audio Laya 99.6-100%, but spam labels are fully confounded with source corpus, and zero-shot transfer of the direct-audio variants to MInDS-14 intents stayed at the majority baseline (accuracy 6.2-8.5%, AUROC 49.0-50.8%) while urgent-clip detection at the default threshold was 9 of 20 (Tables 4.1-4.2, Sec. 4.1).

Jev's accuracy (SST-2 0.961, AG News 0.867) exceeded gpt-5.4-nano (0.948, 0.811), gpt-4.1-nano (0.938, 0.851) and the untrained DeBERTa -c in all 16 wording x rule cells (full-test estimate +5.72 [+4.70, +6.75]), but trailed the task-exposed DeBERTa on AG News (-2.30 [-3.33, -1.28]), and label descriptions alone moved the gap from +6.93 to +9.67 points (Tables 6-8, Sec. 4.3).

Top-label ECE depended on question form and task (SST-2 yes/no 0.091 underconfident, choice 0.020, AG News 0.089 with the middle of the scale overconfident: stated 0.750 vs observed 0.612 on 258 items); one fitted temperature cut held-out ECE to 0.023-0.034, and 71.6% of AG News answers sat at exactly 1.00; no directional calibration claim was possible for gpt-4.1-nano, while gpt-5.4-nano gave the true class zero probability on 216 of 284 errors (Tables 2-4, Sec. 4.1, 4.6).

A 5% automatic tier certified for Jev in 0 of 2,000 AG News splits (DeBERTa -c 23, task-exposed 95) but in 191 of 2,000 SST-2 splits (9.4% traffic automated), conformal single-label answers were wrong 5.93% at a nominal 5%, and 0.01 quantisation left a threshold only 53 operating points, although Jev's risk-coverage area beat -c by 1.81 points [0.84, 2.79] (Tables 5, 9; Sec. 4.4-4.5).

The authors' WEV typed models had ECE 0.024-0.059 on browser steps and 0.033-0.099 out of domain, and a DONE-probability threshold trades premature stops against recall (WEV-4b 8.5% premature at 82% recall at 0.5; 3.8% at 67% at 0.8), but the BLOCKED (give-up) option was recalled on only 3% of 29 test steps for all three sizes (Tables 7, 10; Fig. 3; Sec. 5.4, 5.7).

On 741 federal IT solicitations with quote-derived gold, Jev's primary-class accuracy 91.9% exceeded Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (89.6%) and Laya (78.0%), but on fulfillment mode (n=634) Jev reached 65.0% against Qwen's 71.0% (Laya 45.7%), with configured-build precision 0.254 (README Results table; report Sec. 9.1, 9.3).

Nine Jev variants crossing three question structures (12 presence nouls, one 12-way choice, hierarchical choices) with three input sizes all scored 0.912-0.919 primary-class accuracy (676-681 of 741 correct) with ECE 0.046-0.052 (report Sec. 8.2-8.3).

Jev's primary-class ECE was 0.049 against Laya's 0.322 (median confidence 0.41), while Qwen's three prompt-defined confidence levels gave 90.1% precision on 97.8% of rows; but Jev's fulfillment-mode ECE was 0.125 (report Sec. 9.1-9.3).

Only Jev supported an auto-accept gate: at cutoff 0.94 it accepted 86.5% of rows at 96.7% observed precision (Wilson lower bound >= 95%), whereas no Qwen bucket and no Laya cutoff reached 95%; the cutoff was fitted on the same 741 gold rows, and a spec rule queuing any flag cut automation from 91.9% to 26.6% (README Sec. 1, 5; report Sec. 9.2, 9.6).

Mean accuracy over five public classification benchmarks (CLINC150, MASSIVE ja-JP, tweet_eval emotion and sentiment, Civil Comments insult) was 83.6 for hosted Jev and 84.2 for the author's Reflex-1 against 85.6 / 84.8 for GPT-5.6 / Gemini 3.8, from one sequential run with no per-benchmark tables or intervals in the deposit (README Results table).

The paper reports ECE 0.0228 and Brier 0.0274 for the four-action Jev trading agent on 1,000 frozen BTCUSDT ticks (ECE 0.0546 / 0.0238 / 0.0240 by information level), but it does not define the outcome against which calibration was scored, the text and Table 2 disagree (0.0542/0.0306 vs 0.0546/0.0238), and the LLM comparison is modelled, not measured (Tables 2-3, 7; Sec. 4.1-4.2).

Screening 142,504 records of 22 Cochrane reviews with one Noul question gave median AUC 0.9827 [IQR 0.9541, 0.9925] (above TITAN-SR's reported 0.9760), and the plugin's untuned 0.3 threshold gave pooled recall 0.9349 at specificity 0.8568, but recall reached 99% in only 16 of 22 reviews (as low as 0.6923 and 0.7778, with 16 and 22 missed includes) (report.md primary analysis tables).

On 4,940 ToxicChat examples at a threshold selected on 1,000 development labels, Jev reached 90.52% recall at 3.24% FPR (AP 0.8854, AUROC 0.9849) against 35.63-58.91% recall for three encoder conditions, the only arm to pass the absolute gate, but its FPR on the human-annotated negatives was 5.39% (128/2,376), above the 5% tolerance (Tables R1, R1a, R2).

On 4,000 held-out domain names every probability band was right at least as often as stated, so the probability was conservative rather than calibrated (e.g. band 0.60-0.70: 95% interval of share right 74.5-82.6%; >= 0.95: 99.5% right at mean 0.98) (slide 9).

A gate fixed on 1,000 separate names (keep Jev's rerank at p >= 0.62, else dksplit's first reading) raised held-out accuracy from 90.0% to 92.8% (178 corrected vs 65 broken, McNemar p = 2.5e-13), beat dksplit at every threshold from 0.30 to 0.98, and at p >= 0.90 accepted 53.1% of names at 99.2% precision (slides 6-8).

The author's fine-tuned Laya with retrieval reached F1 0.89 on synthetic logs (rule baseline 0.66; 20 replications), detected 0.92 of an unseen attack, and transferred to CIC-IDS2017 SSH brute force without retuning (F1 0.98-0.99, CI lower bound 0.96 vs rule 0.76), but slow port scans were missed (recall 0.03-0.31 vs rule 0.43) because the synthetic threshold did not transfer, and recall fell to 0.00 without authentication events (Tables 1-2, 7; Sec. 5.6).

In simulated shadow-mode response the fine-tuned detector blocked every attacker (1.00) within a minute, but caused 17 +/- 25 wrongful isolations and 5.5 estimated wrongful block hours per replication; because its false alarms carried high risk scores, risk-scaled cooldowns lengthened wrongful blocking (5.5 vs 2.9 h fixed), so the author keeps shadow mode with human approval as default (Tables 5-6, Sec. 5.5).

Jev classified 41,172 OpenAlex works to build a 14,714-work AI-research panel for 25 Indian institutions at about 13.5% annual growth, but its only check is an 88-record agent-adjudicated set (90.9% agreement overall, 97.2% on the 72 records at p >= 0.75), and admitting lower-confidence labels changes the total by +49.8% (Tables 1, 3; Sec. 2.4, 3.5).
